steps.tx: On angiography, healthy retinal vessels hold their dye in a crisp column, so any blurring of that column deserves attention. Here the vessel walls stain and leak segment by segment, fluorescein escaping into surrounding retina where inflammation has loosened the barrier. That **vascular leakage** pattern confirms active retinal vasculitis rather than an old scarred vessel. Leakage near the macula or disc raises the stakes, pushing management towards systemic immunosuppression instead of watchful waiting with drops alone.
steps.say: Segmental vessel wall staining and dye leakage on angiography prove active retinal vasculitis.
